# Built-in macro definitions

The macros that come with the language, as written in `src/prelude.vidar`. For how to use them, see [Built-in macros](../language/builtin-macros.md). Names are called with a `!`, for example `scoped!`.

### `scoped!`

```odin
scoped :: proc!(allocator: Expr = context.allocator, body: Stmt) -> Stmt
```

```text
scoped! { ... } gives the block its own temp allocator and frees it when the block ends.
scoped!(allocator) { ... } takes the arena's memory from `allocator` instead of context.allocator.
```

### `with_allocator!`

```odin
with_allocator :: proc!(allocator: Expr, body: Stmt) -> Stmt
```

```text
with_allocator!(a) { ... } makes `a` the block's context.allocator.
```

### `locked!`

```odin
locked :: proc!(mutex: Expr, body: Stmt) -> Stmt
```

```text
locked!(&mutex) { ... } holds the lock for the block and releases it on every exit.
```

### `timed!`

```odin
timed :: proc!(label: Expr = "", body: Stmt) -> Stmt
```

```text
timed!("label") { ... } prints how long the block took (to stderr). The label defaults to the call site.
```

### `track!`

```odin
track :: proc!(a: Expr = "", b: Expr = "", body: Stmt) -> Stmt
```

```text
track!("label") { ... } runs the block with a tracking context.allocator and, when it ends, prints
every allocation that is still live (to stderr). The label defaults to the call site.
Only in -debug builds; otherwise the block runs untracked.
track!(allocator) / track!(allocator, "label") tracks allocations made from `allocator` instead.
```

### `do!`

```odin
do :: proc!(T: Type = _, body: Stmt) -> Expr
```

```text
do! { ...; take value } evaluates to the value the block takes. The block runs just before the enclosing
statement. do!(T) { ... } gives the result type when it can't be inferred from the taken values.
```

### `comptime!`

```odin
comptime :: proc!(body: Stmt) -> Expr
```

```text
comptime! { expr } / comptime! { ...; take value } runs the block in the transpiler and folds to its value:
calls in it run at compile time, as if each had a '!'.
```

### `dbg!`

```odin
dbg :: proc!(value: Expr) -> Expr
```

```text
dbg!(expr) prints "file:line: expr = value" (to stderr) and evaluates to the value.
```

### `check!`

```odin
check :: proc!(cond: Expr, message: Expr = "") -> Stmt
```

```text
check!(cond) panics when cond is false, showing the expression; for comparisons it also
shows both operands. check!(cond, "message") adds a message.
```

### `todo!`

```odin
todo :: proc!(message: Expr = "") -> Expr
```

```text
todo!() / todo!("message"): panic in code that isn't written yet.
```

### `unimplemented!`

```odin
unimplemented :: proc!(message: Expr = "") -> Expr
```

```text
unimplemented!() / unimplemented!("message"): panic in code that is deliberately not supported.
```
